items.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I analyzed the concerto by Darius Milhaud, which is basically the first one for percussion and orchestra

ctx.x: I wrote, I analyzed, it’s a history of the percussion concerto, solo percussion and orchestra. So I did a big history of that, I analyzed the concerto by Darius Milhaud, which is basically the first one for percussion and orchestra, and I wrote a concerto and analyzed that, did a performance guide, and there you have it. And I think it put me to sleep by. And somebody at NYU recently came and said, “I checked out your dissertation,” I’m like oh [yawns] enjoy it as much as I did? So it wasn’t really like having…

Well the whole other side of your career, a part of it is as a composer. When you started composing did you find a need to have keyboard skills? Or usually we think of a drummer, unless they go out of their way to get all the harmony study, as maybe not having that as much.
